description: A melanocytic nevus (common mole) is a benign skin lesion caused by a local proliferation of pigment-producing melanocytes. Most adults have 10-40 moles, which mostly appear in childhood and adolescence and continue developing up to around age 40. They can be flat or raised, and range in color from pink/flesh-toned to dark brown, steel blue, or black.
symptoms: Usually a single, even color: brown, tan, black, red, pink, blue, skin-toned, or colorless
Round or oval shape with a smooth, distinct edge
Can be flat or raised/protruding, with a smooth or dome-shaped surface; may have hair growing from it
Usually the size of a pencil eraser or smaller
Can appear anywhere on the skin, including the scalp, between fingers/toes, soles, palms, or under nails
It is normal for new moles to appear in children and teens, and for existing moles to lighten, darken, or fade with age
warning_signs: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, Diameter, Evolving (ABCDE rule)
A mole changing in size, shape, structure, or color
A new mole developing after age 30-40 (sources vary on the exact age threshold)
A mole that looks different from a person's other moles ("ugly duckling" sign)
Dysplastic/atypical features: larger than 5mm, irregular borders, mixed/varied color, or a flat surface with scaly or pebbly texture instead of smooth
recommendation: Perform monthly self-skin examinations and see a dermatologist if a mole starts to grow, itch, bleed, or otherwise change. People with multiple dysplastic nevi (5 or more) are noted to carry meaningfully higher melanoma risk and may need more frequent professional skin exams.
